questions.q: What does hovering a changed line in a pull request's diff reveal?
options: A small icon for leaving a comment attached to that exact line
An automatic approval of the whole pull request
A button that deletes the line
Nothing — GitHub only supports comments on the PR as a whole
questions.explain: Hovering a diff line reveals a comment icon, letting you attach feedback to that exact line rather than the PR in general.

questions.q: What is a 'suggestion' in a GitHub code review, according to this lesson?
options: A line comment that includes an exact, editable fix the author can accept with one click
A vague comment describing that something is wrong without specifics
An automatic merge of the pull request
A private message sent outside of GitHub
questions.explain: A suggestion goes beyond describing a problem — it proposes the exact fix as an editable code block, acceptable with one click.

questions.q: Where do you go to submit a review after leaving line comments?
options: The 'Review changes' button on the Files changed tab
The repository's Settings page
A separate email to the author
The Issues tab
questions.explain: Individual line comments don't do anything until bundled into a review submitted via the Review changes button.

questions.q: Which review verdict actually blocks the merge button until resolved?
options: Request changes
Comment
Approve
None of them block anything
questions.explain: Request changes is the verdict that blocks merging on a repo requiring review, until it's addressed or dismissed.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does the 'Comment' verdict do?
options: Provides feedback with no verdict attached — it doesn't block or approve anything
Immediately blocks the merge
Automatically approves the pull request
Deletes the pull request
questions.explain: Comment is feedback only — it carries no approval or blocking verdict, unlike Approve or Request changes.
